methods.notes: Match the 0xFF00 service. Local names vary widely by pack vendor; the service UUID plus a valid 0xDD/0x77 reply to a 0x03 read is the real discriminator.

device.manufacturer: Shenzhen Jiabaida (JBD) — many LiFePO4 pack rebrands (Overkill Solar, LIONTRON, ECO-WORTHY, ...)
device.name: JBD / Xiaoxiang Smart BMS
device.notes:
JBD (a.k.a. Xiaoxiang) smart battery-management systems ship inside a huge number of LiFePO4/Li-ion packs under many brands. The same frames run over a plug-in BLE module or a UART (9600 8N1). No cloud; read telemetry and, in factory (EEPROM) mode, write protection settings and toggle the charge/ discharge FETs and balancer.
GATT: service 0000ff00-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb; notify (RX) 0000ff01-...; write (TX) 0000ff02-....
FRAME: start 0xDD, then payload, a 2-byte checksum, end 0x77. Checksum = 0x10000 - sum(payload bytes). Command byte 0xA5 = read, 0x5A = write. A read request is [0xDD, 0xA5, register, length, data..., checksum-hi, checksum-lo, 0x77]; a response is [0xDD, register, status (0x00 OK / 0x80 error), length, data..., checksum, 0x77].
KEY REGISTERS:
  0x03 basic info — pack voltage (u16, 10 mV), current (s16, 10 mA, negative
       = discharge), remaining + design capacity (10 mAh), cycle count,
       protection/error flags, software version, SOC %, FET status bits
       (charge/discharge), cell count, NTC count + temps (0.1 K)
  0x04 per-cell voltages (u16 @ 1 mV)
  0x05 device name string
EEPROM config needs factory mode: write 0x56 0x78 to register 0x00; exit via register 0x01. Control registers: 0xE1 MOSFET control (bit0 disable charge FET, bit1 disable discharge FET), 0xE2 balancer control.
Newer firmware may add an authentication exchange (frames starting FF AA ... 77) and a 6-byte password (since firmware 0x16).

openness.notes: Not officially published; the register map was reverse-engineered by the community and multiple implementations agree. The newer-firmware auth handshake internals are the least-settled part.

credentials.notes: No pairing on older firmware; newer firmware may require an authentication exchange and/or a password before writes. Reads are unauthenticated. SAFETY: writing FET-control or protection registers on a live pack is dangerous — treat writes as advanced.

factory_reset.description:
The reason anyone needs this is almost always the same: somebody set a Bluetooth password in the Xiaoxiang app and is now locked out, because that app has no function to remove one. Two escape routes exist and both leave the app behind. JBD's own desktop tool includes a password-clearing function, and the open BMS-Tools desktop application can send a password-reset command; either way a USB communication module is needed, not Bluetooth.
A full factory restore via button presses on the PCB itself is also described by the community, but no reliable sequence was established here — hence low confidence and no steps for it. On a device whose parameters decide whether a lithium pack is protected, a guessed button sequence is not something to publish.
SAFETY: after any restore, verify the cell count, capacity and every protection threshold before reconnecting the pack.
factory_reset.effect: A firmware-level restore returns the BMS to factory defaults, including clearing a Bluetooth password that has been set. Cell configuration and protection parameters go with it — on a battery management system those are safety settings, so this is not a casual operation.

procedures.basis: JBD's desktop tool and the open BMS-Tools application, both documented by the Xiaoxiang/Overkill Solar community as the way out of a password lockout. Requires a USB communication module.
procedures.name: Clear the Bluetooth password over USB

steps.action: Connect a USB communication module to the BMS's UART port.
From JBD's desktop tool or BMS-Tools, issue the password clear / password reset command.
steps.expect: The Bluetooth password is removed and the app connects again.

methods.description: Connect, subscribe to notify char 0xFF01, write commands to 0xFF02. Read 0x03 for basic info and 0x04 for per-cell voltages.

steps.action: Connect and subscribe to the notify characteristic (0xFF01).
Write a 0x03 read to 0xFF02 to get basic info; parse the 0xDD..77 response.

setup.notes: Nothing to provision: connect over BLE, subscribe to the notify characteristic, and write 0xDD-framed read/write commands. Confidence high: the register map is exhaustive and several implementations agree.

rejoin.notes: No network membership; a new BLE client connects independently.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The GATT service/char UUIDs, the 0xDD/0x77 framing, command bytes and register map are from the bms-tools register map and syssi/esphome-jbd-bms / kolins-cz.

characteristics.name: Notify (RX)
characteristics.notes: Responses arrive here: [0xDD, register, status, length, data..., checksum, 0x77].

read_basic_info.description: Read register 0x03 (pack voltage, current, SOC, FET status, temps, flags). Frame: DD A5 03 00 FF FD 77.

read_cell_voltages.description: Read register 0x04 (per-cell voltages, u16 @ 1 mV). Frame: DD A5 04 00 FF FC 77.

read_device_name.description: Read register 0x05 (device name string). Frame: DD A5 05 00 FF FB 77.

services.name: JBD BMS service
services.notes: Notify (RX) on 0xFF01, write (TX) on 0xFF02. All frames are 0xDD ... checksum 0x77; checksum = 0x10000 - sum(payload).
